patients.summary: Retired administrative assistant with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes, hypertension, CKD 3b, rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate and prednisone, severe COPD and GERD who joins in 2019. Osteoporosis, renal secondary hyperparathyroidism, two intubations for COPD, glucocorticoid excess, a stage IB vulvar SCC, a fragility wrist fracture and shingles follow; septic shock in 2026 leaves diffuse renal cortical necrosis and dialysis-dependent ESRD.

documents.author: front desk

Asked her to bring all pill bottles and inhalers.

orders.reason: Rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate, transfer of care

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
65 yo woman transferring care. Retired admin assistant, lives with her husband. Brought every bottle in a shopping bag, which helped.

HPI: Diabetes for about 15 years, never well controlled per her report; on metformin and glyburide, checks sugars maybe twice a week, fasting usually 150s-190s. No lows she knows of. HTN on three agents. Kidney function has been drifting down for a couple of years and she was told stage 3. RA since her mid-50s, hands mostly, on weekly methotrexate and daily prednisone 10 mg from her rheumatologist, whose office is closing to new referrals from her old group so she needs a new one. COPD: never smoked, but has had a bad chest for years; dyspnea on one flight of stairs, uses rescue inhaler a few times a week. Reflux controlled on omeprazole.

PMH: T2DM, HTN, CKD 3b, RA, COPD (severe per prior PFTs), GERD.
PSH: TAH at 52 for fibroids.
Meds: reconciled from bottles, see list. Takes calcium and D because of the prednisone.
Allergies: none to drugs.
FHx: Mother with T2DM and osteoporosis. Father with HTN and COPD. Maternal aunt broke a hip from osteoporosis.
SHx: Never smoker. Wine 1-2 glasses a week. No drugs.

ROS: Chronic exertional dyspnea, morning stiffness in hands ~30 min. Otherwise negative.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Pleasant, in no distress. Lungs with diminished breath sounds at both bases, prolonged expiration, no wheeze today. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft. Hands with mild MCP swelling bilaterally, no warmth. No leg edema. Feet: skin intact, monofilament sensation intact, DP pulses 2+.

A/P:
1. T2DM, poorly controlled - A1c today. Will revisit regimen once labs back; glyburide in her kidney range is not ideal, noted for next visit.
2. HTN - 138/82, near goal on three drugs, continue.
3. CKD 3b - BMP and urine albumin today; referral to nephrology since she has none locally.
4. RA - continues MTX/prednisone; referral to rheumatology for ongoing management and MTX monitoring.
5. COPD - severe by history, continue ICS/LABA and albuterol. Will request old PFTs.
6. GERD - stable.
7. HM - records request for vaccines, colonoscopy, mammogram. HCV screen today. Flu/pneumonia vaccines at a nurse visit next month.

Return 3 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Beverly, your labs from Tuesday are back. A1c is 8.9, which tells me your sugars have been running high for a while; we'll talk about options at your December visit, and in the meantime cutting back on the evening snacks we discussed will help. Kidney function is about where your old records put it (creatinine 1.35), and there is protein in the urine (ratio 210), which is common with diabetic kidney disease. Your blood count, liver tests and cholesterol are fine. Hepatitis C screen is negative. The nephrology office should call you to schedule.

reports.text: Pre- and post-bronchodilator spirometry. Acceptable and reproducible efforts. Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.56. Post-bronchodilator FEV1 41% predicted. No significant bronchodilator response.
Bilateral screening mammogram. Scattered fibroglandular densities. No suspicious mass, calcification or architectural distortion.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records received from prior primary care office, 64 pages, covering 2014-2019. Scanned. Pertinent items abstracted:
- PFTs 3/2017: severe obstruction, FEV1 41% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.56 post-BD.
- Screening colonoscopy 2016: normal to the terminal ileum, no polyps; repeat in 10 years.
- Mammogram 5/2018: BI-RADS 1.
- Tdap 6/2015; PCV13 10/2018; flu shots yearly.
- Problem list matches what she reported. Creatinine 1.2-1.4 range over 2017-2019.
- No drug allergies documented.

documents.title: Nurse visit - immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for flu and pneumococcal vaccines per PCP. PCV13 documented in outside records 10/2018, so PPSV23 due. Screened, no contraindications. High-dose flu L deltoid, PPSV23 R deltoid. Tolerated. VIS given. Waited 15 min, no reaction.

documents.title: Nephrology consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outpatient Nephrology Consultation
Date of service: 10/30/2019
Reason: CKD 3b, referred by her primary care physician.

Thank you for sending Ms. Fischer, a 65 year old woman with long-standing type 2 diabetes, hypertension, RA on methotrexate and prednisone, and severe COPD. Creatinine has risen from about 1.2 to 1.35 over two years. Urine albumin to creatinine ratio 210 mg/g. No hematuria. No NSAID use. BP 136/80 here.

Impression: CKD stage 3b, most consistent with diabetic and hypertensive kidney disease, moderately increased albuminuria.

Recommendations: Continue lisinopril. Avoid NSAIDs and IV contrast where possible. I would watch metformin dosing as filtration falls. Methotrexate is renally cleared; rheumatology aware. We will see her yearly with labs beforehand.

Meds reviewed: metformin, glyburide, lisinopril, amlodipine, HCTZ, omeprazole, prednisone, methotrexate, fluticasone-salmeterol, albuterol, aspirin, calcium, vitamin D3.
Allergies: NKDA.

Outside Nephrology Group

documents.title: Rheumatology new patient consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY CONSULTATION - 11/19/2019

65F with seropositive RA for about ten years, transferring care. Currently methotrexate 15 mg weekly and prednisone 10 mg daily. Reports 30 minutes of morning stiffness, no recent flares. Exam: mild synovial thickening at MCPs 2-3 bilaterally, no active synovitis, no deformity. Disease activity low.

CKD 3b noted; we will keep MTX at 15 mg and monitor CBC, LFTs and creatinine every 3 months - your office's draws are fine, please copy us. Prednisone is also covering her lung disease per her account; no change today.

Plan: continue current regimen, return 1 year or sooner for flare.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here for 3-month follow-up. Saw nephrology and rheumatology, letters reviewed, no changes from either. Says she has been better about portion size; still having toast and jam at night sometimes. Home fasting sugars 140s-180s. No hypoglycemia. Breathing at baseline.

O: Vitals as charted. Lungs diminished, no wheeze. RRR. No edema.

A/P:
- T2DM, not at goal. A1c and MTX monitoring labs today. Discussed that glyburide is a concern with her kidneys; she would rather not change anything before the holidays. Will look at the full picture at her wellness visit in February.
- HTN controlled.
- CKD 3b, nephrology following.
- RA, labs drawn for rheum.
- Eye exam: she says she saw her optometrist last week, will get the report.
RTC February for annual wellness visit.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Dilated eye examination, exam date 12/3/2019. VA 20/25 OD, 20/25 OS with correction. Pupils and pressures normal. Lens: early nuclear sclerosis both eyes. Fundus: no diabetic retinopathy, no macular edema either eye. Recommend repeat dilated exam in 12 months.

documents.body: Electronic request from pt's pharmacy for glyburide 5 mg #90 and lisinopril 20 mg #90. Last filled by prior PCP. Sent 90-day supplies with 1 refill per PCP. Pt has AWV 2/17.

orders.reason: Height loss; long-term prednisone; family history of osteoporosis

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual wellness visit, combined with diabetes follow-up and a full medication reconciliation (she brought the bag again).

Meds reviewed one by one against pharmacy fill history: all 13 being taken as listed. Uses spacer? No - DPI, technique observed and fine.

Diabetes: still not at goal. Diet changes partial. We talked about adding a DPP-4 inhibitor, which is safe at her kidney function and doesn't cause lows. She wants to give diet three more months before adding a pill, and is worried about another copay. Fair enough; revisit.

Health risk assessment: lives with husband in a two-story house, independent in ADLs and IADLs, drives. No falls in past year. Hearing fine. Advance directive: has health care proxy (husband), copy requested.

Bones: she mentions her clothes fit differently and she thinks she has shrunk - measured height today is shorter than the 5'4" she reports from her 50s. Ten-plus years of prednisone, mother with osteoporosis, aunt with hip fracture. No DXA in old records. Ordered.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Lungs with distant breath sounds. Heart regular. Mild MCP thickening. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses palpable, no ulcers.

Screening: mammogram due 5/2020, will order. Colonoscopy 2016 normal. HCV done. Pneumococcal complete. Flu done.

Plan: labs today, DXA, mammogram this spring. Follow-up after DXA.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 9.1 - a bit higher than September. Kidney numbers stable. Cholesterol and blood counts OK. The bone density scan order is in; radiology will call. -your PCP

documents.title: RE: Lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. I know the sugar is my fault. I'm going to try harder with the evening eating before we add anything. Bev

documents.title: Check-in call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Outreach call to high-risk patients during the pandemic. Pt staying home, husband doing the shopping. Breathing at baseline, has albuterol and 2 months of her controller. Asked about switching to 90-day mail order - set up for metformin, amlodipine, HCTZ, omeprazole. Reminded her not to stop prednisone. Bone density scan was postponed by radiology; they will call to reschedule. Knows to call us for fever or worse breathing.

reports.study: DXA bone density, hip and spine
reports.text: Dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry of the lumbar spine (L1-L4) and left hip. No artifacts limiting interpretation. Lumbar spine L1-L4: T-score -2.8. Left total hip and femoral neck measured; the lumbar spine is the lowest site. WHO classification based on the lowest T-score.
reports.conclusion: Osteoporosis. Lowest T-score -2.8 at the lumbar spine.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth once weekly in the morning with a full glass of plain water, 30 minutes before food or other medicines; stay upright for 30 minutes

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Bone Density
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
In person, masked, first in-office visit since March.

S: Follow-up on DXA. She has never broken a bone that she knows of. Estimates she has lost about 2 inches (5 cm) over several years. No back pain episodes. No falls.

Data: DXA 4/28: L1-L4 T -2.8, lowest site. Labs drawn 5/12: calcium, phosphorus, intact PTH and alk phos all within normal limits, so no secondary bone disease evident on labs.

A/P: Osteoporosis - glucocorticoid exposure plus postmenopausal, strong family history. Start alendronate 70 mg weekly; went through the dosing routine twice (empty stomach, 8 oz plain water, sit or stand 30 minutes, nothing else first). Her reflux is controlled; she will tell me about any heartburn or swallowing trouble. Keep calcium and D3 but not within the alendronate window. Dental check fine per her. Repeat DXA in 2 years.

T2DM - diet effort ongoing, next A1c in summer.
RTC August (video OK).

documents.title: Question about the new bone pill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Can I take the new weekly pill on the same morning as my methotrexate? Right now I take both on the same morning.

documents.title: RE: Question about the new bone pill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Good question. Simplest is to move the alendronate to a different morning of the week, first thing with water only. Keep your methotrexate day the same. Call with any heartburn.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison 5/2018. Scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No suspicious masses, calcifications or distortion. Stable.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt in her kitchen, husband helped with the camera. Consent for video obtained.

Labs from 8/13 reviewed with her. A1c still well above goal. She has been walking the driveway loop most days, weight steady by her scale. Tolerating alendronate, no heartburn. Breathing ok in the humidity, using albuterol a few times a week.

We returned to the question of a third diabetes drug; she still prefers to hold off. Agreed to recheck in the fall. Kidney labs stable. MTX labs fine, copied to rheum.

Flu shot at a nurse visit in late September. RTC November in person.

documents.title: Flu vaccine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: High-dose flu vaccine L deltoid, lot recorded. No prior reactions. VIS given. Pt waited in car 15 min per curbside protocol, no issues.

documents.title: Nephrology follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Nephrology Clinic Follow-up, 10/20/2020 (telephone visit due to pandemic).

CKD 3b, diabetic/hypertensive. Labs from her PCP in August reviewed: creatinine within her recent range, potassium normal. BP at home 130s/80s. No new NSAIDs. Started alendronate this spring for osteoporosis; acceptable at her current filtration, would stop if eGFR falls below 30.

Plan: continue current regimen. PTH and phosphorus with next labs. Return in one year.

Outside Nephrology Group

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Diabetes/CKD f/u. Feels more tired this fall than usual, attributes to staying in and the short days. Some achiness in shins and hips, worse in the evening. No fevers, no weight loss. Breathing baseline.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs distant. No synovitis today. No edema.

A/P: T2DM - A1c today; she continues to decline adding a medication for now. CKD - labs. Fatigue/achiness - will see what labs show; if persistent, broader workup. RTC 2 months or sooner.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body: Rheumatology follow-up 11/24/2020. RA quiet. Morning stiffness brief. No synovitis on exam. Monitoring labs from PCP office reviewed, acceptable. Continue methotrexate 15 mg weekly and prednisone 10 mg daily. Follow up 1 year.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Annual dilated diabetic eye exam, 12/1/2020. Corrected acuity 20/25 both eyes. IOP normal. Mild nuclear sclerosis, stable. Retina: no diabetic retinopathy, no macular edema. Return 1 year.
